clue.text: A record-spinner on American list must be flexible

parts.note: a disc jockey, DJ, spins records
a table is a list set out in rows, as in a league table

explanation.surface: A disc jockey working off an American playlist has to be ready to adapt.
explanation.definitionFit: Something adjustable can be altered to suit, so it is flexible in the sense of adaptable.

clue.text: Offer money being sensitive and vulnerable

definitions.meaning: to ... is to offer payment formally, as when ... the exact fare
... as an adjective means sore or easily hurt, as with a ... bruise

explanation.surface: Someone holds out cash while feeling exposed and easily hurt.
explanation.definitionFit: One word covers both senses: the verb for formally presenting payment, and the adjective for something sore and easily damaged.

clue.text: I like this poet's new elementary forms

parts.note: so can mean in this way, as in 'do it so'

indicators.note: new tells us the letters of poet's are made into a fresh arrangement

explanation.surface: A poet's admirer claims to like the poet's fresh, basic verse forms.
explanation.definitionFit: Isotopes are variant forms of a chemical element, so they are literally forms of elements, punned on as 'elementary'.

clue.text: Has a think after answer provides entertainment

indicators.note: after shows that the thinking word comes after the abbreviation for answer

parts.note: to muse is to ponder or think something over

explanation.surface: Someone mulls over a reply, and the result proves entertaining.
explanation.definitionFit: To amuse someone is to entertain them, so the verb in the third person matches 'provides entertainment'.

clue.text: Provided timers intermittently after gaffer loses head and becomes inflexible

indicators.note: after places the decapitated gaffer before the rest, as the rest comes after it
loses head says the first letter of the word for gaffer is dropped

parts.note: a gaffer is a boss, the person in charge of a workplace
provided, as in 'provided that', means if

indicators.note: intermittently means only every other letter of timers is taken

explanation.surface: A foreman, short of time-keepers, grows set in his ways.
explanation.walkthrough: 'loses head' drops the first letter of the word for gaffer; 'intermittently' takes the even letters of timers; 'after' sets the shortened gaffer first.
explanation.definitionFit: To ossify is literally to turn into bone, and figuratively to become rigid and unwilling to change.

clue.text: Importance of mine host, originally

parts.note: a pit is a coal mine

indicators.note: originally means only the first letter of host is used

explanation.surface: A question about how much the landlord of the pub at the mine matters.
explanation.definitionFit: Pith is the essential core of something, hence its substance or significance.

clue.text: Deal with a shift Boxing Day

indicators.note: boxing means enclosing, so the word for shift holds the day abbreviation inside it

parts.note: a shift is a loose straight dress

explanation.surface: Someone must tackle a work shift on Boxing Day, the British holiday the day after Christmas.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Boxing Day' reads as the December 26th holiday; here 'Boxing' puts D inside DRESS.
explanation.definitionFit: To address a problem is to tackle it or attend to it.

clue.text: Life making old man upset about island

indicators.note: about means the rearranged letters go around the island abbreviation
upset means the letters of making old man are knocked into a new order

explanation.surface: Moving to an island has unsettled an elderly man.
explanation.walkthrough: 'upset' rearranges MAKING OLD MAN and 'about' wraps those letters round I.
explanation.definitionFit: The animal kingdom is the whole category of animal life in biological classification.

clue.text: Essentially female row about small dog

indicators.note: essentially points to the core, the two central letters of female

parts.note: S is the usual abbreviation for small, as on clothing labels
a tiff is a petty quarrel, a row

explanation.surface: A woman argues about a little dog.
explanation.definitionFit: A mastiff is a large, powerful breed of dog.

clue.text: Person with unique conviction — posh chap employed by dispatcher of trees

parts.note: fir is a kind of tree; the plural is read as 'fir' with the sender's S following

indicators.note: employed by means the posh chap is taken into the work of, so placed within, the other pieces

parts.note: a sender dispatches things
a toff is an upper-class man

explanation.surface: A man in court for one crime turns out to be a toff working for a timber firm.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dispatcher of trees' suggests a lumberjack, but it is a tree plus a sender; 'employed by' sets the posh chap inside that, just after the S.
explanation.definitionFit: A first offender has a single conviction to their name, so their conviction is unique.

clue.text: One sister is courting floods

parts.note: the Roman numeral I is one
a nun is a religious sister
dates means goes out with, is courting

explanation.surface: One nun is seeing someone romantically.
explanation.definitionFit: To inundate is to overwhelm with water, so the verb with its -s ending matches floods.

clue.text: Allergenic hormones will limit secretion from a wound

indicators.note: limit means hold within bounds, so the letters sit inside the outer words

explanation.surface: Hormones triggering allergy will restrict the fluid oozing from a cut.
explanation.definitionFit: Ichor, besides the blood of the gods in Greek myth, is a thin watery discharge from a wound or ulcer.

clue.text: Person taking part from atomic pile without engineers

indicators.note: without means the engineers' letters are removed

parts.note: an atomic pile is an early name for a nuclear reactor
RE stands for the Royal Engineers, a corps of the British Army

explanation.surface: Someone involved in a nuclear plant that has no engineers.
explanation.definitionFit: An actor plays a part in a play, so is literally someone taking part; actor also means a participant.

clue.text: Catching mum, keeping time after exercise

indicators.note: after shows the word for mum with its insert follows the exercise abbreviation

parts.note: PE is physical education, school exercise

indicators.note: keeping means holding, so the word for mum holds the time abbreviation

parts.note: mum, as in 'keep mum', means silent

explanation.surface: Mum caught something, but keeps time after her workout.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mum' looks like mother but means SILENT; 'keeping' puts T inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Pestilent means spreading disease, so in the sense of infectious it matches catching.

clue.text: Speaks in support of European party and explains

indicators.note: in a down clue a word in support of others sits below them, so this comes after

parts.note: Lab is short for the UK Labour Party
orates means gives a speech

explanation.surface: A politician gives speeches backing a European party and sets out its case.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in support of' places ORATES beneath E + LAB in this down answer.
explanation.definitionFit: To elaborate is to explain in more detail or develop a point.

clue.text: Weirdly, likes hoarding books in buckets

indicators.note: hoarding means storing away, so the jumbled letters keep the books inside
weirdly shows the letters of likes come out in a strange order

parts.note: B is book, so two books are BB

explanation.surface: Someone oddly fond of stashing books in pails.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Weirdly' rearranges likes into KILES, and 'hoarding' holds the two books inside it. A kibble is a mining bucket.
explanation.definitionFit: A kibble is a large iron bucket used in mining and wells for raising ore or water.

clue.text: Prisoners split by scramble for lots

indicators.note: split by means the word for prisoners is broken open with the other word inside

parts.note: lag is slang for a convict, so lags are prisoners
to shin is to scramble or climb up, as in shinning up a pole

explanation.surface: Convicts are divided by a rush for the prize draw.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lots' looks like the lottery picture of 'scramble'; it is an informal word for plenty.
explanation.definitionFit: Lashings is informal British for a large quantity, as in lashings of cream.

clue.text: Regularly admit employees on mother's side

indicators.note: regularly means every other letter of admit is taken

parts.note: staff are the employees of a firm

explanation.surface: A firm routinely takes on workers from the maternal line.
explanation.definitionFit: The distaff side of a family is the female line, from the spindle once used for women's spinning.

clue.text: Turkey, cutting unusual duties, must get whatever remains

indicators.note: cutting means the Turkey code goes into the rearranged letters
unusual means the letters of duties are given an odd arrangement

parts.note: TR is the international vehicle code for Turkey

explanation.surface: Turkey, slashing odd tariffs, must accept what is left over.
explanation.walkthrough: 'unusual' rearranges duties into DEITUS, and 'cutting' places the vehicle code for Turkey inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Detritus is debris or waste matter, the leftovers when something breaks down.

clue.text: Reportedly rub son in dirt — if necessary!

indicators.note: reportedly means the word for rub is used for its sound, as if heard

parts.note: to knead is to work or rub with the hands

indicators.note: in places the son abbreviation inside the word for dirt

parts.note: smut is soot or dirt

explanation.surface: Supposedly a parent will scrub their son's face in the mud if they have to.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Reportedly' gives NEED, the sound of KNEAD; 'in' puts S into SMUT to make SMUST.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom 'needs must' says something has to be done because circumstances demand it, close to 'if there is no choice'.

clue.text: Raise right, perhaps favourable aspect

parts.note: to up something, as in up the price, is to raise it
right is an example of a side, as with left and right; perhaps signals the example

explanation.surface: A question of raising someone's pay, perhaps with a good angle on it.
explanation.definitionFit: The upside of a situation is its positive side, its advantage.

clue.text: Bankrupt, having left for right man

indicators.note: left for right means one abbreviation takes the place of the other

parts.note: broke means out of money

explanation.surface: Someone ruined after quitting a rightward political stance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'left for right' swaps L in for R in BROKE.
explanation.definitionFit: Bloke is informal British for a man, a chap.

clue.text: Businessman's initial stretch for violation

indicators.note: initial means only the first letter of businessman's is used

parts.note: reach as a noun is an extent or stretch, as in a reach of a river

explanation.surface: A company boss's opening stretch of power ends in a rules violation.
explanation.definitionFit: A breach is a breaking of a rule, law or agreement, as in breach of contract.

clue.text: Cover from banned hot issue

indicators.note: from means the letters are taken out of the run of words that follows

explanation.surface: A news cover story about a forbidden controversial topic.
explanation.definitionFit: A dhoti is a loincloth worn by men in India, a garment that covers the lower body.

clue.text: Sound name adopted by social inferior

indicators.note: adopted by means the name abbreviation is taken in by the slang word

parts.note: oik is British slang for a coarse or lower-class person

explanation.surface: A sensible name is taken on by a lowly person.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sound' looks like an adjective (sensible) but is the noun: the noise a pig makes.
explanation.definitionFit: Oink is the grunting noise of a pig.

clue.text: Aromatic plant or dark pine cultivated on east of Alps

indicators.note: on means the rearranged letters come straight after the Alps letter
on a map east is the right-hand side, so this is the final letter of Alps
cultivated means the letters of dark pine are worked over into a new order

explanation.surface: A fragrant plant or a dark pine tree grown on the eastern side of the Alps.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cultivated' rearranges DARK PINE into PIKENARD, placed 'on' the S that 'east of Alps' gives.
explanation.definitionFit: Spikenard, also called nard, is a Himalayan plant yielding a costly aromatic oil.

clue.text: Dealt with a poor horse during medical

indicators.note: during means the horse pieces fall within the word for medical

parts.note: a nag is a worn-out horse

explanation.surface: A vet coped with a sickly horse at its check-up.
explanation.definitionFit: To have managed something is to have handled or coped with it.

clue.text: Vague relation has another, discontented

parts.note: an uncle is a family relation

indicators.note: discontented means emptied of contents, so only the outside letters of another remain

explanation.surface: One relative lives with another who is unhappy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'discontented' looks like 'unhappy' but leaves only the first and last letters, AR.
explanation.definitionFit: Unclear means not plain or definite, the same as vague.
